claims.text: An in-situ laser remelting pass immediately after deposition will improve the mechanical integrity of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
In-situ laser remelting will reduce residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
In-situ laser remelting will minimize elemental segregation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
In-situ laser remelting will heal processing defects in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventionally additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits compositional segregation.
Conventionally additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits high residual stress.
Conventionally additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits processing defects.
Localized remelting dissolves and homogenizes segregated phases in AlCrFeNiSi.
The remelting thermal cycle relaxes residual stresses through partial annealing.
Localized remelting reduces defect connectivity by healing microstructural imperfections.
Controlled resolidification after remelting minimizes defect formation.
Controlled remelting produces a more compositionally uniform microstructure.
Controlled remelting produces finer grains.
Relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, remelted samples will contain fewer processing defects.
Relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, remelted samples will have higher yield strength.
Relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, remelted samples will have improved ductility.
The proposed effects are limited to laser-based additive manufacturing operated within a controlled parameter window and atmosphere.
Direct empirical evidence for in-situ laser remelting of AlCrFeNiSi is currently lacking.
Optimal laser-remelting parameters for AlCrFeNiSi are uncertain.
Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in residual stress, microstructural homogenization, and mechanical performance relative to an untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.
